summary: A narrator sees his friend Lou taken to hospital after an injury, then returns home near dawn and books a morning flight. His suspicion has grown that Alex Goddard's Children of Light and its Guatemalan accomplices are illegally obtaining white babies, and with the Army involved and his sister Sarah now taken, he feels intense guilt for having drawn her into the danger. The excerpt ends with him preparing to wake Steve and make up for past neglect of Sarah.
one_line: The narrator, after Lou's hospital visit, books a flight amid suspicions that Children of Light is trafficking babies and has kidnapped Sarah.
key_facts: Lou is given a sedative by the nurses and is too far gone to answer the narrator's last words.
The narrator is told he can visit Lou anytime after two P.M. the next day, since visiting hours are over.
The narrator takes a cab downtown after the hospital to retrieve his Toyota.
The time is two-fifteen in the morning when the narrator gets home.
The narrator calls American Airlines and books a flight for the morning at nine-thirty.
The narrator now believes Alex Goddard's Children of Light and its Guatemalan accomplices are completely illegal, not merely shady.
The narrator says the group is getting hundreds of white babies in ways that could not bear the light of day.
The group is prepared to do whatever it takes to stop the narrator from highlighting them in his film.
With the Army involved and Sarah taken, the narrator feels the group's game is becoming kidnapping.
The narrator describes Sarah as a pawn, and says this happened because of him.
The narrator's guilt is an intensified version of guilt he has felt for the past fifteen years.
The narrator missed Sarah's high school graduation because he was cramming for grad school finals.
The narrator resolves to start making it up to Sarah and to wake Steve.
Lou mentions 26 Federal Plaza, where the narrator is told to call the next morning.
